claim: The sgn3 mutant displays a dramatic defect in endodermal barrier formation, as visualized by penetration of the apoplastic tracer propidium iodide (PI) into the stele along the entire length of the root.
source: In a forward genetic, GUS-based screen for endodermal barrier mutants (Lee et al., 2013) (Alassimone et al., unpublished), we discovered one mutant, sgn3 that displayed a dramatic defect in endodermal barrier formation, as visualized by penetration of the apoplastic tracer propidium iodide (PI) into the stele along the entire length of the root.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental observation using propidium iodide as a tracer, as described in the text and shown in Figure 1A.

claim: SGN3 encodes a leucine-rich-repeat receptor-like kinase (LRR-RLK) of subfamily XI.
source: SGN3 encodes for a leucine-rich-repeat receptor-like kinase (LRR-RLK) of subfamily XI that had previously been described as GASSHO1 (GSO1) (Figure 1B, Figure 1—figure supplement 2, Figure 1—source data 1) (Tsuwamoto et al., 2008).
evidence: The claim is supported by sequencing data and complementation analysis, with reference to previous characterization by Tsuwamoto et al., 2008.

claim: The Casparian strip in sgn3 mutants is still formed and correctly positioned, but is repeatedly interrupted, forming irregularly-sized 'holes' of several micrometer in length.
source: In order to investigate the cause of this phenotype, we investigated formation of the Casparian strip and found that it is still formed and correctly positioned, but that it is repeatedly interrupted, forming irregularly-sized 'holes' of several micrometer in length (Figure 1C, Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy observations of Casparian strip autofluorescence shown in Figure 1C and Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Suberin lamellae formation in sgn3 mutants appeared at a position and in a manner very similar to wild type.
source: Suberin lamellae formation, by contrast, appeared at a position and in a manner very similar to wild type (Figure 1D,E, Figure 1—figure supplement 1C,D).
evidence: The claim is supported by Fluorol yellow staining data shown in Figure 1D,E and Figure 1—figure supplement 1C,D.

claim: In the sgn3 background, CASP1-GFP showed a pattern of interrupted patches that was strikingly similar to that of the Casparian strip itself.
source: In the sgn3 background, CASP1-GFP showed a pattern of interrupted patches that was strikingly similar to that of the Casparian strip itself.
evidence: The claim is supported by confocal microscopy observations of CASP1-GFP localization shown in Figure 1F.

claim: The incorrect localization of the CASPs causes the Casparian strip defects of the sgn3 mutant.
source: This suggests that it is the incorrect localization of the CASPs that causes the Casparian strip defects of the mutant (Figure 1F).
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that CASP1-GFP localization defects mirror Casparian strip defects.

claim: In a novel forward genetic screen scoring for mutants with altered CASP1-GFP localization, 14 novel alleles of sgn3 were found.
source: Interestingly, in a novel forward genetic screen in which we scored directly for mutants with altered CASP1-GFP localization (Kalmbach et al., unpublished), we found 14 novel alleles of sgn3 (Figure 1B, Figure 1—figure supplement 2, Figure 1—source data 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by data from a forward genetic screen, with alleles documented in Figure 1B and Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: SGN3 is one of the major non-redundant genes necessary for CASP localization in the Arabidopsis genome.
source: This suggests that SGN3 is one of the major non-redundant genes necessary for CASP localization in the Arabidopsis genome.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the discovery of 14 novel alleles in a screen for CASP localization defects.

claim: All four other CASPs (CASP2-5) display identical defects in sgn3.
source: We could show that not only CASP1-GFP, but all four other CASPs (CASP2-5) display identical defects in sgn3 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: The claim is supported by confocal microscopy data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1E.

claim: An interrupted CSD abolishes the lateral diffusion barrier in the plasma membrane of endodermal cells.
source: An interrupted CSD should abolish the lateral diffusion barrier in the plasma membrane of endodermal cells that we had previously described (Alassimone et al., 2010). Indeed, a generic plasma membrane protein that is excluded from the CSD in wild type (Alassimone et al., 2010) (Figure 1G) shows a pattern of exclusion in the mutant that represents a perfect negative image to the CASP1-GFP islands (Figure 1G).
evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy observations of plasma membrane marker localization shown in Figure 1G, with reference to previous work by Alassimone et al., 2010.

claim: The lateral diffusion barrier between inner and outer plasma membrane domain is absent in sgn3 mutants.
source: This illustrates that the lateral diffusion barrier between inner and outer plasma membrane domain is absent in sgn3 mutants, but that the remaining CSD islands are still able to exclude other proteins.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that a generic plasma membrane marker shows exclusion patterns that are the negative image of CASP1-GFP islands.

claim: The defect in lateral diffusion barrier did not affect the polar localization of PDR6, a transporter that localizes to the outer polar domain in the endodermis.
source: To our surprise, this defect did not affect the polar localization of PDR6, a transporter that localizes to the outer polar domain in the endodermis (Figure 1H).
evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy observations of PDR6-Venus localization shown in Figure 1H.

claim: A strict polarity in the endodermis can be maintained in the absence of a diffusion barrier.
source: This indicates that a strict polarity in the endodermis can be maintained in the absence of a diffusion barrier, further supporting the notion that polarity of transmembrane proteins in plants might simply be maintained by generally low lateral diffusion, high rates of endocytosis, or both (Geldner, 2009).
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that PDR6 maintains polar localization in sgn3, with reference to previous work by Geldner, 2009.

claim: During endodermal differentiation, CASP1-GFP changes from a protein that displays endocytic cycling and lateral diffusion to one that is highly stable and immobile in the CSD.
source: We had shown previously that during endodermal differentiation, CASP1-GFP changes from a protein that displays endocytic cycling and lateral diffusion to one that is highly stable and immobile in the CSD (Roppolo et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by reference to previous work by Roppolo et al., 2011.

claim: CASP1-GFP localization passes through a 'string of pearls' stage, in which individual islands or 'patches' of CASP1-GFP are aligned in a band before eventually fusing.
source: In this process, CASP1-GFP localization passes through a 'string of pearls' stage, in which individual islands or 'patches' of CASP1-GFP are aligned in a band before eventually fusing (Figure 2A).
evidence: The claim is supported by time-lapse microscopy observations shown in Figure 2A.

claim: sgn3 is not able to progress from the 'string of pearls' stage, but only undergoes partial fusion of individual islands, leading to CASP1-GFP patches of heterogenous size.
source: Comparison of 3D-time-lapse observations of endodermal differentiation revealed that sgn3 is not able to progress from this 'string of pearls' stage, but only undergoes partial fusion of individual islands, leading to CASP1-GFP patches of heterogenous size (Figure 2A).
evidence: The claim is supported by 3D time-lapse confocal microscopy data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: CASP1-GFP islands in sgn3 have similar stability and turnover as wild type.
source: We further found by fluorescence recovery after photobleaching (FRAP) that these CASP1-GFP islands have similar stability and turnover as wild type (Figure 2B).
evidence: The claim is supported by FRAP experiments shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The CSD shows very strong adherence to the cell wall, leading to the long-described phenomenon of 'band plasmolysis' in endodermal cells.
source: Another feature of the CSD is its very strong adherence to the cell wall, leading to the long-described phenomenon of 'band plasmolysis' in endodermal cells (Krömer, 1903; Behrisch, 1926; Alassimone et al., 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by references to historical observations (Krömer, 1903; Behrisch, 1926) and recent work (Alassimone et al., 2010).

claim: sgn3 showed the inability of CASP1-GFP to retract from the strips upon plasmolysis, demonstrating that plasma membrane-to-cell wall attachment remains intact in the mutant.
source: sgn3 showed the very same inability of CASP1-GFP to retract from the strips, demonstrating that plasma membrane-to-cell wall attachment remains intact in the mutant (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by plasmolysis experiments shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: sgn3 does not cause a general defect in CASP1-GFP trafficking, polymerization or cell wall attachment, but rather a specific defect in the progression of already stable CASP islands towards a contiguous band.
source: We conclude that sgn3 does not cause a general defect in CASP1-GFP trafficking, polymerization or cell wall attachment, but rather a specific defect in the progression of already stable CASP islands towards a contiguous band.
evidence: The claim is inferred from multiple observations: normal CASP stability (FRAP), normal cell wall attachment (plasmolysis), but defective fusion of CASP islands.

claim: SGN3 expression in endodermal cells shortly after the onset of elongation precedes the onset of CASP1 expression.
source: In transgenic lines of this construct, expression of SGN3 could be observed in endodermal cells shortly after the onset of elongation, preceding the onset of CASP1 expression (Figure 2C, Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy observations of SGN3-mVenus expression shown in Figure 2C and Figure 2—figure supplement 3.

claim: The early expression of SGN3 before CASP1 is consistent with a function of SGN3 in establishing correct CASP1 localization.
source: This is consistent with a function of SGN3 in establishing correct CASP1 localization.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the temporal sequence of SGN3 and CASP1 expression.

claim: Initially, SGN3 could be found on all cell sides, but it then quickly accumulated in the transversal and anticlinal sides of the plasma membrane, yet became excluded from the CSD itself.
source: Initially, SGN3 could be found on all cell sides, but it then quickly accumulated in the transversal and anticlinal sides of the plasma membrane, yet became excluded from the CSD itself—a hitherto unknown subcellular localization pattern (Figure 2D–F).
evidence: The claim is supported by confocal microscopy observations of SGN3-mVenus localization shown in Figure 2D–F.

claim: In 3D-reconstructions, SGN3 localization leads to the appearance of a broader ring-like domain that flanks the more restricted, median CSD.
source: In 3D-reconstructions this leads to the appearance of a broader ring-like domain that flanks the more restricted, median CSD (Figure 2F).
evidence: The claim is supported by 3D confocal microscopy reconstructions shown in Figure 2F.

claim: During the critical phase of CASP domain progression from isolated islands towards a fused ring, SGN3 is seen to surround individual CASP islands on all sides.
source: During the critical phase of CASP domain progression from isolated islands towards a fused ring—at which the sgn3 phenotype becomes apparent–SGN3 is seen to surround individual CASP islands on all sides (Figure 2G).
evidence: The claim is supported by confocal microscopy observations shown in Figure 2G.

claim: SGN3 localization surrounding CASP islands would fit with a role of SGN3 in promoting fusion of growing CASP islands, such that an uninterrupted band can be formed.
source: Such localization would fit with a role of SGN3 in promoting fusion of growing CASP islands, such that an uninterrupted band can be formed (Figure 2H).
evidence: The claim is a speculative interpretation of the localization data, illustrated in the model shown in Figure 2H.

claim: ESB1 is an extracellular protein that localizes to the site of Casparian strip formation.
source: ESB1 is an extracellular protein that localizes to the site of Casparian strip formation and whose absence causes a phenotype resembling that of sgn3 insofar as both the Casparian strip itself and CASP1-GFP are localized in interrupted bands (Hosmani et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by reference to previous work by Hosmani et al., 2013.

claim: In contrast to sgn3, esb1 mutants additionally display increased, delocalized deposition of additional autofluorescent cell wall material as well as enhanced and earlier deposition of suberin.
source: In contrast to sgn3, however, esb1 mutants additionally display increased, delocalized deposition of additional autofluorescent cell wall material as well as enhanced and earlier deposition of suberin (Hosmani et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by reference to previous work by Hosmani et al., 2013.

claim: ESB1-mCherry in sgn3 is both present and correctly localized, specifically accumulating at the remaining CASP1-GFP islands.
source: We found ESB1-mCherry in sgn3 to be both present and correctly localized, that is, specifically accumulating at the remaining CASP1-GFP islands (Figure 3A).
evidence: The claim is supported by confocal microscopy observations of ESB1-mCherry localization shown in Figure 3A.

claim: ESB1 does not require SGN3 for its accumulation and localization.
source: Thus, ESB1 does not require SGN3 for its accumulation and localization and the Casparian strip discontinuities in esb1 and sgn3 might be caused by independent mechanisms.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that ESB1 localizes correctly in sgn3 mutants.

claim: The Casparian strip discontinuities in esb1 and sgn3 might be caused by independent mechanisms.
source: Thus, ESB1 does not require SGN3 for its accumulation and localization and the Casparian strip discontinuities in esb1 and sgn3 might be caused by independent mechanisms.
evidence: The claim is speculative, inferred from the observation that ESB1 localizes correctly in sgn3.

claim: sgn3 esb1 double mutant formed less and/or smaller Casparian strip patches than each single mutant, indicating additivity of the two mutations in this common aspect of their phenotypes.
source: Consistently, we found that sgn3 esb1 double mutant formed less and/or smaller Casparian strip patches than each single mutant, indicating additivity of the two mutations in this common aspect of their phenotypes (Figure 3B,C).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantification of Casparian strip presence shown in Figure 3B,C.

claim: sgn3 esb1 double mutants neither display an increased or delocalized deposition of autofluorescent cell wall material, nor an enhanced and earlier formation of suberin.
source: Intriguingly however, sgn3 esb1 double mutants neither display an increased or delocalized deposition of autofluorescent cell wall material, nor an enhanced and earlier formation of suberin.
evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy observations and suberin staining shown in Figure 3B,D.

claim: sgn3 is fully epistatic over esb1 for the phenotype of enhanced and ectopic formation of autofluorescence and suberin.
source: This indicates a full epistasis of sgn3 over esb1 for this phenotype (Figure 3B,D).
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that the double mutant lacks the enhanced suberin phenotype of esb1.

claim: The same epistatic relationship was found between sgn3 and casp1 casp3 double mutants.
source: The same epistatic relationship was found between sgn3 and casp1 casp3 double mutants (Figure 3B–D).
evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy observations and quantification shown in Figure 3B–D.

claim: The enhanced and ectopic formation of autofluorescence and suberin is thought to be due to a feedback and crosstalk between cell wall components, connecting correct Casparian strip formation to the further deposition of lignin and suberin lamellae formation.
source: The enhanced and ectopic formation of autofluorescence and suberin is thought to be due to a feedback and crosstalk between cell wall components, connecting correct Casparian strip formation to the further deposition of lignin and suberin lamellae formation (Hosmani et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by reference to previous work by Hosmani et al., 2013.

claim: The epistasis of sgn3 suggests that the perception/signaling that leads to enhanced autofluorescence and suberin formation in esb1 and casp1 casp3 is mediated by—or at least requires—the SGN3 receptor-like kinase.
source: The epistasis of sgn3 suggests that the perception/signaling that leads to enhanced autofluorescence and suberin formation in esb1 and casp1 casp3 is mediated by—or at least requires—the SGN3 receptor-like kinase.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the epistatic relationship observed in double mutants.

claim: sgn3 displays a rather mild growth phenotype under certain conditions despite the strength of the barrier phenotype and its inability to initiate potentially compensatory suberization.
source: Considering the strength of the barrier phenotype of sgn3 and its inability to initiate potentially compensatory suberization, we were surprised to observe a rather mild growth phenotype of sgn3 under certain conditions (Figure 4A, Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by growth observations shown in Figure 4A and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claim: sgn3 growth is extremely sensitive to changes in environmental conditions that are non-stressful to wild type.
source: Yet we noticed that sgn3 growth is extremely sensitive to changes in environmental conditions that are non-stressful to wild type (Figure 4A, Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by growth observations under different conditions shown in Figure 4A and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The endodermal barrier phenotype persisted in developed root systems of rosette stage plants both on soil and on hydroponics.
source: We ensured that the endodermal barrier phenotype persisted in developed root systems of rosette stage plants both on soil and on hydroponics, thus excluding that the weak phenotype is caused by an eventual repair of the barrier in older plants (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by propidium iodide permeability assays shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Growth differences between sgn3 and wild type are more pronounced at higher temperature, as well as under long-day conditions.
source: A systematic variation of day length, temperature, and light-intensity revealed that growth differences to wild type are more pronounced at higher temperature, as well as under long-day conditions (Figure 4B, Figure 4—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantification of shoot fresh weight under different growth conditions shown in Figure 4B and Figure 4—figure supplement 1C.

claim: CASP1::SGN3-GFP sgn3 plants could fully rescue the growth phenotype of sgn3 plants.
source: These CASP1::SGN3-GFP sgn3 plants could fully rescue the growth phenotype of sgn3 plants (Figure 4C), demonstrating that it is the root endodermal defect of sgn3 that is causative for the overall growth defect of the mutant.
evidence: The claim is supported by growth phenotype observations and fresh weight measurements shown in Figure 4C.

claim: It is the root endodermal defect of sgn3 that is causative for the overall growth defect of the mutant.
source: These CASP1::SGN3-GFP sgn3 plants could fully rescue the growth phenotype of sgn3 plants (Figure 4C), demonstrating that it is the root endodermal defect of sgn3 that is causative for the overall growth defect of the mutant.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the rescue experiment showing that endodermis-specific expression of SGN3 is sufficient to restore normal growth.

claim: The numerous, repeated Casparian strip discontinuities in sgn3 must generate an apoplastic bypass for both water and solutes in the mutant root.
source: The numerous, repeated Casparian strip discontinuities in sgn3 must generate an apoplastic bypass for both water and solutes in the mutant root.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the structural defects observed in the Casparian strip.

claim: Transpiration rate per surface area in sgn3 mutants are very similar to wild type.
source: We observed that transpiration rate per surface area in sgn3 mutants are very similar to wild type (Figure 4D) revealing that there is no compensatory downregulation of transpiration.
evidence: The claim is supported by transpiration measurements shown in Figure 4D.

claim: There is no compensatory downregulation of transpiration in sgn3 mutants.
source: We observed that transpiration rate per surface area in sgn3 mutants are very similar to wild type (Figure 4D) revealing that there is no compensatory downregulation of transpiration.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that transpiration rates are similar to wild type.

claim: Root pressure, as estimated by xylem sap exudation from hypocotyls after decapitation, was lower in the sgn3 mutant.
source: We indeed found that root pressure, as estimated by xylem sap exudation from hypocotyls after decapitation, was lower in the sgn3 mutant (Figure 4E).
evidence: The claim is supported by xylem sap exudation measurements shown in Figure 4E.

claim: sgn3 showed a decreased rate of leaf guttation, a process more indirectly dependent on root pressure.
source: sgn3 also showed a decreased rate of leaf guttation, a process more indirectly dependent on root pressure, but that can be observed less invasively (Figure 4F).
evidence: The claim is supported by guttation measurements shown in Figure 4F.

claim: sgn3 mutants show a significant increase in root hydrostatic hydraulic conductivity (Lpr-h) compared to wild type.
source: As a more direct measure of apoplastic water flow, we inserted excised roots in a pressure chamber and found a significant increase in root hydrostatic hydraulic conductivity (Lpr-h) in sgn3 mutants compared to wild type (Figure 4G).
evidence: The claim is supported by hydraulic conductivity measurements shown in Figure 4G.

claim: The defects of Casparian strip formation may allow an apoplastic bypass for water in pressurized sgn3 roots thereby explaining its increased Lpr-h.
source: The defects of Casparian strip formation may allow an apoplastic bypass for water in pressurized sgn3 roots thereby explaining its increased Lpr-h.
evidence: The claim is a speculative interpretation of the increased hydraulic conductivity data.

claim: The findings are the first genetic evidence that Casparian strips can be relevant for root pressure buildup and impose a hydraulic resistance.
source: Our findings are the first genetic evidence that Casparian strips can be relevant for root pressure buildup and impose a hydraulic resistance; the magnitude of the observed effects nevertheless indicates that an intact Casparian strip is not an absolute requirement and that unmodified walls and/or suberized cells can generate a sufficiently high resistance to radial waterflow so that the positive root pressure can be maintained.
evidence: The claim is based on the water transport measurements in sgn3 mutants.

claim: An intact Casparian strip is not an absolute requirement for root pressure, and unmodified walls and/or suberized cells can generate a sufficiently high resistance to radial waterflow so that positive root pressure can be maintained.
source: Our findings are the first genetic evidence that Casparian strips can be relevant for root pressure buildup and impose a hydraulic resistance; the magnitude of the observed effects nevertheless indicates that an intact Casparian strip is not an absolute requirement and that unmodified walls and/or suberized cells can generate a sufficiently high resistance to radial waterflow so that the positive root pressure can be maintained.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that sgn3 mutants still maintain some root pressure despite lacking intact Casparian strips.

claim: All of the seven more highly expressed genes in sgn3 were found to be also induced by potassium starvation, suggesting a latent, weak potassium deficiency stress under these conditions.
source: Only little differences between sgn3 and wild type were observed. Yet, all of the seven more highly expressed genes in sgn3 were found to be also induced by potassium starvation, suggesting a latent, weak potassium deficiency stress under these conditions (Figure 5A, Figure 5—source data 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by microarray data shown in Figure 5A and analysis using Genevestigator.

claim: Both AKT1 and HAK5, well-established transcriptional read-outs of potassium deficiency in roots, were upregulated in sgn3.
source: Based on this indication, we tested well-established transcriptional read-outs of potassium deficiency in roots, the potassium influx transport proteins AKT1 and HAK5, and found that both were upregulated in sgn3 (Figure 5B,C).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative RT-PCR data shown in Figure 5B,C.

claim: Concentrations of most elements remained essentially unaltered in sgn3 despite the dramatic apoplastic bypass in sgn3 roots.
source: Surprisingly, concentrations of most elements remained essentially unaltered in sgn3. Despite the dramatic apoplastic bypass in sgn3 roots, the mutants managed to maintain wild type levels of sodium (Na), calcium (Ca), or boron (B), for example.
evidence: The claim is supported by ionomic analysis data shown in Figure 5D and Figure 5—source data 2.

claim: sgn3 mutants managed to maintain wild type levels of sodium (Na), calcium (Ca), or boron (B).
source: Despite the dramatic apoplastic bypass in sgn3 roots, the mutants managed to maintain wild type levels of sodium (Na), calcium (Ca), or boron (B), for example.
evidence: The claim is supported by ionomic analysis data shown in Figure 5D and Figure 5—source data 2.

claim: Among the measured transition elements (Mo, Co, Mn, Zn, Fe, Cu, Zn) only zinc showed a significant decrease in some measurements.
source: Among the measured transition elements (Mo, Co, Mn, Zn, Fe, Cu, Zn) only zinc showed a significant decrease in some measurements (Figure 5D, Figure 5—source data 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by ionomic analysis data shown in Figure 5D and Figure 5—source data 2.

claim: Lower levels of potassium (K) were invariably found in the sgn3 mutant (ranging from 1.4–3.0 fold reduction).
source: However, matching the transcriptional profiling results, we invariably found lower levels of potassium (K) in the mutant (ranging from 1.4–3.0 fold reduction).
evidence: The claim is supported by ionomic analysis data shown in Figure 5D and Figure 5—source data 2.

claim: Levels of magnesium (Mg) and cesium (Cs) accumulated to higher levels than in wild type, ranging from 1.5–2.1 and 1.3- to 1.4-fold increase, respectively.
source: Inversely, levels of magnesium (Mg) and cesium (Cs) accumulated to higher levels than in wild type, ranging from 1.5–2.1 and 1.3- to 1.4-fold increase, respectively (Figure 5D, Figure 5—source data 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by ionomic analysis data shown in Figure 5D and Figure 5—source data 2.

claim: Wild type plants coped well with conditions of low potassium nutrition, with most plants displaying no or only very weak chlorosis on older rosette leaves.
source: Wild type plants coped well with conditions of low potassium nutrition, with most plants displaying no or only very weak chlorosis on older rosette leaves, indicative of potassium deficiency (Figure 5E,F).
evidence: The claim is supported by growth observations under low potassium conditions shown in Figure 5E,F.

claim: Wild type maintained higher potassium concentration than sgn3 under low potassium conditions.
source: Consistently, wild type also maintained higher potassium concentration than sgn3 under these conditions (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by ionomic analysis under low potassium conditions shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: The sgn3 mutant developed severe chlorosis of its rosette leaf margins under low potassium conditions, characteristic of strong potassium deficiency.
source: The sgn3 mutant in contrast, developed severe chlorosis of its rosette leaf margins, characteristic of strong potassium deficiency (Marschner and Marschner, 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by growth observations shown in Figure 5E,F, with reference to Marschner and Marschner, 2012.

claim: sgn3 has an impaired capacity to accumulate sufficient potassium under conditions of low supply of this element.
source: sgn3 therefore has an impaired capacity to accumulate sufficient potassium under conditions of low supply of this element.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the severe potassium deficiency symptoms observed in sgn3 under low potassium conditions.

claim: The sgn3 mutant represents a powerful new tool to better understand root uptake and transport mechanism of most other plant nutrients.
source: The sgn3 mutant represents a powerful new tool to better understand root uptake and transport mechanism of most other plant nutrients as well.
evidence: The claim is a speculative statement about the potential utility of the mutant for future research.

claim: The initial analysis of the sgn3 mutant challenges the current notions of the role of the Casparian strip as a required barrier for most or all elements.
source: Our initial analysis of the sgn3 mutant challenges the current notions of the role of the Casparian strip as a required barrier for most or all elements.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that most elements maintain homeostasis in sgn3 despite the barrier defect.

claim: Potassium is the only macronutrient (N,P,K,S) that is not integrated into polymers and that remains highly mobile within the plants.
source: Potassium (K) is the only macronutrient (N,P,K,S) that is not integrated into polymers and that remains highly mobile within the plants.
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge about potassium biochemistry in plants.

claim: Potassium is being used as a counter ion in many transport process and is recycled back to the root along with the phloem sap.
source: It is being used as a counter ion in many transport process and is recycled back to the root along with the phloem sap.
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge about potassium transport in plants.

claim: Concentrations of potassium required for plant growth are high and potassium often needs to be concentrated 10–100 fold over the concentration found in the soil.
source: At the same time, concentrations of potassium required for plant growth are high and potassium often needs to be concentrated 10–100 fold over the concentration found in the soil (Marschner and Marschner, 2012; Wang and Wu, 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by references to Marschner and Marschner, 2012 and Wang and Wu, 2013.

claim: It makes sense that potassium is an element that cannot be kept at sufficiently high levels in Casparian strip defective plants.
source: It therefore makes a lot of sense that potassium is an element that cannot be kept at sufficiently high levels in Casparian strip defective plants.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the properties of potassium and the observations in sgn3.

claim: Potassium located in the stelar apoplast is continuously lost to the outer cell layers and the soil in the absence of functional Casparian strips.
source: We propose that potassium located in the stelar apoplast is continuously lost to the outer cell layers and the soil in the absence of functional Casparian strips.
evidence: The claim is a speculative model proposed to explain the potassium deficiency in sgn3.

claim: Upregulation of potassium influx carriers in cortex/epidermis would be able to recuperate large parts of the potassium being lost.
source: Upregulation of potassium influx carriers in cortex/epidermis, as we have observed in sgn3 roots, would certainly be able to recuperate large parts of the potassium being lost.
evidence: The claim is a speculative interpretation of the observed upregulation of potassium transporters.

claim: A chronic condition of very low external potassium would lead to a breakdown in transporter-mediated 'potassium recycling' and eventually cause the deficiency phenotypes observed.
source: However, a chronic condition of very low external potassium would lead to a breakdown in this transporter-mediated 'potassium recycling' and eventually cause the deficiency phenotypes that we observe.
evidence: The claim is a speculative model proposed to explain the potassium deficiency phenotype in sgn3 under low potassium conditions.

claim: There should be a higher rate of potassium flux out-of and into the root stele in a sgn3 mutant.
source: From this scenario, it follows that there should be a higher rate of potassium flux out-of and into the root stele in a sgn3 mutant and that potassium homeostasis in the mutant is extremely dependent on increased activity of potassium transporters.
evidence: The claim is a prediction derived from the proposed 'potassium recycling' model.

claim: Potassium homeostasis in the sgn3 mutant is extremely dependent on increased activity of potassium transporters.
source: From this scenario, it follows that there should be a higher rate of potassium flux out-of and into the root stele in a sgn3 mutant and that potassium homeostasis in the mutant is extremely dependent on increased activity of potassium transporters.
evidence: The claim is a prediction derived from the proposed 'potassium recycling' model.

claim: An increase in the levels of magnesium could be explained by a lower concentration gradient between the xylem sap and the external environment and a lower mobility of Calcium within the cell wall space.
source: This could be explained by a lower concentration gradient between the xylem sap and the external environment and a lower mobility of Calcium within the cell wall space (Clarkson, 1984; White and Broadley, 2003).
evidence: The claim is a speculative explanation for the differential effects on magnesium vs. calcium, with references to Clarkson, 1984 and White and Broadley, 2003.

claim: Calcium delivery to aerial tissues is thought to occur either entirely through the apoplast or to employ a very short symplastic route passing exclusively through endodermal cells.
source: Therefore, calcium delivery to aerial tissues is thought to occur either entirely through the apoplast–using the few apoplastic 'bypasses' of the endodermis at the root tip or at lateral root emergence sites (White, 2001)—or to employ a very short symplastic route passing exclusively through endodermal cells (Clarkson, 1984).
evidence: The claim is based on established models of calcium transport, with references to White, 2001 and Clarkson, 1984.

claim: It is surprising that the opening of a massive apoplastic bypass in the sgn3 mutant has no effect on calcium homeostasis, while it did affect levels of magnesium.
source: In both scenarios, it is surprising that the opening of a massive apoplastic bypass in the sgn3 mutant has no effect on calcium homeostasis, while it did affect levels of magnesium.
evidence: The claim is an observation that challenges current understanding of calcium transport.

claim: Magnesium is more mobile in the apoplast than Calcium and undergoes increased apoplastic transport into the transpiration stream in sgn3.
source: Possibly, magnesium is more mobile in the apoplast than Calcium and undergoes increased apoplastic transport into the transpiration stream in sgn3 (Thibault and Rinaudo, 1985).
evidence: The claim is a speculative explanation for the differential effects on magnesium vs. calcium, with reference to Thibault and Rinaudo, 1985.

claim: The endodermis represents the main barrier to extracellular diffusion in plant roots.
source: The endodermis represents the main barrier to extracellular diffusion in plant roots, and it is central to current models of plant nutrient uptake.
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge about root anatomy and function.

claim: SGN3/GASSHO1 is a receptor-like kinase that is necessary for localizing CASPARIAN STRIP DOMAIN PROTEINS (CASPs) into an uninterrupted, ring-like domain.
source: We show that SGN3/GASSHO1 is a receptor-like kinase that is necessary for localizing CASPARIAN STRIP DOMAIN PROTEINS (CASPs)—major players of endodermal differentiation—into an uninterrupted, ring-like domain.
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple lines of experimental evidence including localization studies and mutant analysis.

claim: SGN3 appears to localize into a broader band, embedding growing CASP microdomains.
source: SGN3 appears to localize into a broader band, embedding growing CASP microdomains.
evidence: The claim is supported by confocal microscopy observations shown in Figure 2D-G.

claim: The sgn3 mutant demonstrates a major defect in maintaining sufficient levels of the macronutrient potassium.
source: We observe a surprising ability of the mutant to maintain nutrient homeostasis, but demonstrate a major defect in maintaining sufficient levels of the macronutrient potassium.
evidence: The claim is supported by ionomic analysis and potassium deficiency experiments shown in Figure 5.

claim: The plant root is a highly selective filter that forages the soil environment for nutrients and water.
source: The plant root is a highly selective filter that forages the soil environment for nutrients and water.
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge about root function.

claim: The function of roots has been likened to that of an 'inverted gut', displaying a very similar dual role in uptake and protection.
source: Its function has been likened to that of an 'inverted gut', displaying a very similar dual role in uptake and protection (Waisel et al., 2002).
evidence: The claim is supported by reference to Waisel et al., 2002.

claim: Selectivity of roots is thought to crucially depend on the endodermis.
source: Selectivity of roots is thought to crucially depend on the endodermis, an inner cell layer that surrounds the central vascular strand of the root and represents the main paracellular (apoplastic) transport barrier in young roots (Geldner, 2013).
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge with reference to Geldner, 2013.

claim: The apoplastic diffusion barrier is set up by the 'Casparian strips', lignin-like, hydrophobic impregnations of the primary cell wall that form a supracellular net-like structure around the central vasculature.
source: This apoplastic diffusion barrier is set up by the 'Casparian strips', lignin-like, hydrophobic impregnations of the primary cell wall that form a supracellular net-like structure around the central vasculature.
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge about Casparian strip structure.

claim: The net-like arrangement of Casparian strips provides a seal of the extracellular space, while still allowing for nutrient and water transport across outer and inner plasma membrane surfaces.
source: In analogy to the tight junction of gut epithelia, this net-like arrangement provides a seal of the extracellular space, while still allowing for nutrient and water transport across outer and inner plasma membrane surfaces.
evidence: The claim is based on established understanding of Casparian strip function.

claim: The Casparian strip-bearing endodermis represents an independent development of a polarized epithelium, evolved in the context of multi-cellular organisms with wall-bearing cells.
source: The Casparian strip-bearing endodermis therefore represents an independent development of a polarized epithelium, evolved in the context of multi-cellular organisms with wall-bearing cells.
evidence: The claim is based on evolutionary and comparative biology knowledge.

claim: Later during endodermal development, hydrophobic (cork-like) suberin lamellae form all around the endodermal surface.
source: Later during endodermal development, hydrophobic (cork-like) suberin lamellae form all around the endodermal surface.
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge about endodermal development.

claim: Protective suberization should eventually abolish direct transport across the endodermal plasma membrane, forcing symplastic passage through plasmodesmata from outer cell layers.
source: This protective suberization should eventually abolish direct transport across the endodermal plasma membrane, forcing symplastic passage through plasmodesmata from outer cell layers.
evidence: The claim is based on established understanding of suberin function.

claim: A family of previously undescribed four-transmembrane-span proteins, called CASPs, forms a central, ring-like membrane domain in the endodermis, called the Casparian strip membrane domain (CSD).
source: Recent papers established that a family of previously undescribed four-transmembrane-span proteins, called CASPs, forms a central, ring-like membrane domain in the endodermis, called the Casparian strip membrane domain (CSD).
evidence: The claim is supported by references to recent publications on CASPs.

claim: The CSD acts as a lateral diffusion barrier and separates the endodermal plasma membrane into two distinct polar domains.
source: This domain acts as a lateral diffusion barrier and separates the endodermal plasma membrane into two distinct polar domains (Roppolo et al., 2011; Alassimone et al., 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by references to Roppolo et al., 2011 and Alassimone et al., 2010.

claim: Upon localization, the CASPs show extreme stability and a lack of endocytosis or lateral diffusion.
source: Upon localization, the CASPs show extreme stability and a lack of endocytosis or lateral diffusion.
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge from previous CASP studies.

claim: CASPs show extensive pair-wise interactions and associate strongly with cell walls.
source: Moreover, CASPs show extensive pair-wise interactions and associate strongly with cell walls.
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge from previous CASP studies.

claim: Multiple knock-outs of CASP family members display strongly disorganized formation of Casparian strips, demonstrating their functional importance.
source: Multiple knock-outs of CASP family members display strongly disorganized formation of Casparian strips, demonstrating their functional importance.
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge from previous CASP studies.

claim: The CASPs act as scaffolds that spatially organize cell wall biosynthetic enzymes.
source: It is thought that the CASPs act as scaffolds that spatially organize cell wall biosynthetic enzymes.
evidence: The claim is a model based on previous research on CASPs.

claim: CASP1 was shown to determine the subcellular localization of a secreted peroxidase, PER64.
source: CASP1 was shown to determine the subcellular localization of a secreted peroxidase, PER64 (Lee et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by reference to Lee et al., 2013.

claim: In current models, the role of CASPs is to assemble a specific NADPH oxidase with peroxidases, leading to oxidation of mono-lignols and local polymerization of lignin.
source: In current models, the role of CASPs is to assemble a specific NADPH oxidase with peroxidases, leading to oxidation of mono-lignols and local polymerization of lignin.
evidence: The claim is based on current models of Casparian strip formation.

claim: ENHANCED SUBERIN 1 (ESB1), a dirigent-like protein is a cell wall protein that has been demonstrated to be crucial for the correct formation of Casparian strips.
source: Lignin formation in vivo must implicate numerous other cell wall proteins and ENHANCED SUBERIN 1 (ESB1), a dirigent-like protein is a cell wall protein that has also been demonstrated to be crucial for the correct formation of Casparian strips (Hosmani et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by reference to Hosmani et al., 2013.

claim: Multiple mutants of the CASP family display interrupted Casparian strips in the beginning, but rather quickly deposit more cell wall material in a delocalized fashion, eventually sealing the apoplast.
source: Multiple mutants of the CASP family display interrupted Casparian strips in the beginning, but rather quickly deposit more cell wall material in a delocalized fashion, eventually sealing the apoplast.
evidence: The claim is based on observations of CASP mutant phenotypes.

claim: Both CASP mutants and esb1 mutant display an earlier and stronger production of suberin lamellae.
source: Moreover, both mutants display an earlier and stronger production of suberin lamellae (esb1 was named based on this phenomenon).
evidence: The claim is based on observations of CASP and esb1 mutant phenotypes.

claim: In the rbohf mutant, the Casparian strip defect is only partial and restricted to the young part of the root.
source: In the rbohf mutant, the Casparian strip defect is only partial and restricted to the young part of the root.
evidence: The claim is based on observations of rbohf mutant phenotype, with reference to Lee et al., 2013.

claim: RBOHF has roles in many different aspects of plant development.
source: Moreover, RBOHF has roles in many different aspects of plant development and it would be hard to distinguish what phenotype is directly caused by defects in Casparian strip formation (Lee et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by reference to Lee et al., 2013.

claim: SGN3 loss-of-function leads to the strongest defects in Casparian strips known to date.
source: SGN3 loss-of-function leads to the strongest defects in Casparian strips known to date, with no indication of a compensatory upregulation of suberin, as seen for other mutants (Hosmani et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by comparison of sgn3 phenotype with other Casparian strip mutants, with reference to Hosmani et al., 2013.

claim: The sgn3 mutant shows no indication of a compensatory upregulation of suberin, as seen for other mutants.
source: SGN3 loss-of-function leads to the strongest defects in Casparian strips known to date, with no indication of a compensatory upregulation of suberin, as seen for other mutants (Hosmani et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by suberin staining data shown in Figure 1D,E, with reference to Hosmani et al., 2013.

claim: The analysis reveals a surprising capacity of the sgn3 mutant to maintain homeostatic control in the absence of the major root diffusion barrier.
source: Our analysis reveals a surprising capacity of the mutant to maintain homeostatic control in the absence of the major root diffusion barrier and challenges views according to which the root should lose its ability for selective nutrient uptake, because of a generalized, non-selective bypass of nutrients into the vasculature.
evidence: The claim is supported by ionomic analysis showing maintenance of most element concentrations in sgn3.

claim: The sgn3 mutant challenges views according to which the root should lose its ability for selective nutrient uptake, because of a generalized, non-selective bypass of nutrients into the vasculature.
source: Our analysis reveals a surprising capacity of the mutant to maintain homeostatic control in the absence of the major root diffusion barrier and challenges views according to which the root should lose its ability for selective nutrient uptake, because of a generalized, non-selective bypass of nutrients into the vasculature.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that most elements maintain homeostasis in sgn3 despite the barrier defect.

claim: Only a C-terminal mVenus fusion with a 9.4-kb genomic fragment containing intron, 5′UTR, and the upstream neighboring gene, provided full complementation of the sgn3 mutant phenotype.
source: Only a C-terminal mVenus fusion with a 9.4-kb genomic fragment containing intron, 5′UTR, and the upstream neighboring gene, provided full complementation of the mutant phenotype, indicating functionality of the protein fusion and of its regulatory sequences (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A,B).
evidence: The claim is supported by complementation data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2A,B.

claim: The C-terminal mVenus fusion construct indicates functionality of the protein fusion and of its regulatory sequences.
source: Only a C-terminal mVenus fusion with a 9.4-kb genomic fragment containing intron, 5′UTR, and the upstream neighboring gene, provided full complementation of the mutant phenotype, indicating functionality of the protein fusion and of its regulatory sequences (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A,B).
evidence: The claim is inferred from the successful complementation of the mutant phenotype.
